headline: 84 detained as DB uncovers drug den at DIG’s house
summary: Detective Branch of the police has raided a residence belonging to a Deputy Inspector General, uncovering a drug den within the premises.
details: The Detective Branch (DB) of the police conducted a raid on the house of a Deputy Inspector General (DIG) of police, uncovering a drug den operating from the premises.
During the operation, authorities detained 84 individuals suspected of being involved in the drug trade or using the premises for illegal activities.
The raid was carried out following specific intelligence regarding the illegal activities taking place at the residence.
Further investigations are underway to determine the extent of the drug operation and the role of the police officer involved.
caption:

The raid was carried out following specific intelligence regarding the illegal activities taking place at the residence.

headline_marked: Freedom fighter and artist [[Saida Kamal buried with state honors]]
headline: Freedom fighter and artist Saida Kamal buried with state honors
summary: The 74-year-old artist and 1971 liberation war veteran served injured fighters in India's Tripura during the war.
details: Freedom fighter and artist Saida Kamal was laid to rest with state honors on Tuesday afternoon at the Azimpur Graveyard in Dhaka.
Police officers provided a guard of honor during the burial ceremony, which was attended by her family, including her elder sister and human rights activist Sultana Kamal.
The 74-year-old artist passed away last Sunday morning at a private hospital in the capital while suffering from pneumonia and kidney complications.
Born in 1952, Saida Kamal graduated in Drawing and Painting from the Faculty of Fine Arts at Dhaka University.
During the 1971 Liberation War, she worked alongside her sister Sultana Kamal at the Bangladesh Field Hospital in Tripura, India, serving injured freedom fighters.
For her contributions during the war, she received a special commendation letter from the Supreme Commander of the Liberation War.
Beyond her wartime service, she was a renowned artist and teacher, with several solo and joint art exhibitions held both in Bangladesh and abroad.
caption:
A veteran of the 1971 Liberation War and a renowned artist, Saida Kamal has been laid to rest with state honors.

Freedom fighter and artist Saida Kamal was laid to rest with state honors on Tuesday afternoon at the Azimpur Graveyard in Dhaka.

Police officers provided a guard of honor during the burial ceremony, which was attended by her family, including her elder sister and human rights activist Sultana Kamal.

The 74-year-old artist passed away last Sunday morning at a private hospital in the capital while suffering from pneumonia and kidney complications.

Born in 1952, Saida Kamal graduated in Drawing and Painting from the Faculty of Fine Arts at Dhaka University.

During the 1971 Liberation War, she worked alongside her sister Sultana Kamal at the Bangladesh Field Hospital in Tripura, India, serving injured freedom fighters.

For her contributions during the war, she received a special commendation letter from the Supreme Commander of the Liberation War.

Beyond her wartime service, she was a renowned artist and teacher, with several solo and joint art exhibitions held both in Bangladesh and abroad.
